$comment: Relations and facts between realms on 20 September 1378 for the east (DIPL-020, SETUP-022), in the 1444 shape; entities: landless 1378 actors; obedience: each Catholic realm's Pope in the Schism (rome or avignon).

relations.explanation: Tributary since 1373; Andronikos IV owes his throne (Aug 1376) to Murad, pays tribute and handed back Gallipoli (1376-77). Byzantium is in civil war: John V and Manuel II are imprisoned in the Anemas tower and escape to Murad in June 1379.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium
Inalcik, The Ottoman Empire: The Classical Age

historical_end.how: Tarnovo taken by Bayezid; Shishman executed 1395.

relations.explanation: Ivan Shishman is Murad's vassal; his sister Kera Tamara is in Murad's household as a pledge. The date of submission is disputed (c.1371-1376).
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium
Inalcik, The Ottoman Empire: The Classical Age

historical_end.how: Marko killed at Rovine fighting for Bayezid; land annexed.

relations.explanation: Marko Kraljević of Prilep, Ottoman vassal since the Maritsa (26 Sep 1371); his land is shown as Ottoman.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

historical_end.how: Constantine killed at Rovine; land annexed.

relations.explanation: Constantine Dragaš of Velbužd (Kumanovo, Štip, Strumica), Ottoman vassal since the Maritsa; his land is shown as Ottoman.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

historical_end.how: John V restored; Genoa and Byzantium fight over Pera until 1381.

relations.explanation: Genoa (Pera) put Andronikos IV on the throne and was promised Tenedos.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

historical_end.how: John V restored with Venetian ships.

relations.explanation: Venice backs the imprisoned John V and holds Tenedos against Andronikos IV's grant of it to Genoa.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium
Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Despot Manuel Kantakouzenos holds the Morea as an autonomous despotate accepted by John V.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Francesco I Gattilusio holds Lesbos by imperial grant (1355).
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Alexios Angelos Philanthropenos rules Thessaly with the Byzantine title of caesar; the tie is nominal.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Lazar and Tvrtko destroyed Nikola Altomanović together (1373); Lazar accepted Tvrtko's Serbian crown (1377).
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Vuk Branković is Lazar's son-in-law and ally.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

historical_end.how: Balša II killed at Savra by Ottoman troops called in by Karl Thopia.

relations.explanation: Balša II wants Durrës and the lead of Albania; Karl Thopia holds central Albania. Balša takes Durrës in 1385 and dies at Savra.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Prizren and the Kosovo border, taken from the Balšići c.1376-77.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Tvrtko took Trebinje, Konavle and Dračevica from the Balšići (1377) and wants Kotor and the coast.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Half-brothers Shishman and Sratsimir rule rival tsardoms; Vidin also broke from the Tarnovo patriarchate.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Louis the Great held Vidin 1365-1369, then restored Sratsimir as his vassal.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Ragusa under Hungarian protection since the Treaty of Zadar (1358); pays tribute.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Hungarian suzerainty is claimed but not exercised; Radu I acts freely (Louis's campaign c.1377, low).
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

historical_end.how: Peace between Ivanko and Genoa.

relations.explanation: Long naval conflict between Dobrotitsa and the Genoese of the Black Sea.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

relations.explanation: Albanian clans under Gjin Bua Shpata press Ioannina; Thomas Preljubović calls in the Ottomans c.1380.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

historical_end.how: Heredia ransomed.

relations.explanation: Grand Master Heredia's expedition to Epirus ended with his capture by Gjin Bua Shpata (1378, month uncertain); ransomed 1379.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium
Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

historical_end.how: Navarrese Company takes over Achaea.

relations.explanation: Joanna I of Naples is Princess of Achaea; the principality is leased to the Hospitallers (1377-1381).
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

historical_end.how: Lease ends; Navarrese rule.

relations.explanation: Five-year Hospitaller lease of Achaea from Joanna I (1377-1381).
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: The Navarrese Company serves in Hospitaller pay in 1378 (location medium); it takes Thebes in 1379 and Achaea from 1381.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Byzantine-Latin frontier in the Peloponnese.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium
Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: The Tocco count palatine of Cephalonia holds by Angevin grant; Carlo I Tocco is a boy under his mother Maddalena Buondelmonti.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

historical_end.how: Catalans recognise Peter IV of Aragon.

relations.explanation: The Catalan duchy's duchess is Maria of Sicily; vicar-general Luis Fadrique. Peter IV of Aragon claims it and is accepted by the Catalans in 1379-80.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: County of Salona under the Fadrique, a fief of the Catalan duchy.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Marquisate of Bodonitsa under the Zorzi, a fief of the duchy (also tied to Venice).
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Duke Niccolò III dalle Carceri under Venetian protection.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Smyrna split since the crusade of 1344: the harbour castle Hospitaller, the upper castle Aydın's; long low-level war.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

historical_end.how: Peace with Genoa to free James I.

relations.explanation: Genoa holds Famagusta since 1374; a Cypriot attempt on it in 1378 (medium).
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Peter II marries Valentina Visconti, daughter of Bernabò (1378); an anti-Genoese tie.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Cypriot fortress of Korykos (Gorhigos) on the Cilician coast, held since 1361.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

relations.explanation: Over the Hamid lands and the lead of Anatolia.
sources: Inalcik, The Ottoman Empire: The Classical Age

relations.explanation: A marriage of Bayezid with Devlet Hatun of Germiyan is being made; the Kütahya dowry is dated 1381 by the chronicles (1378 in some works).
sources: Inalcik, The Ottoman Empire: The Classical Age

relations.explanation: Karaman covets Beyşehir and resents Hamid's sale of its towns to Murad.
Over Kayseri.
Former Eretnid governors at Erzincan, nearly independent.
Ghars al-Din Khalil, Mamluk vassal, often rebellious; murdered 1386.
Ramadanid lords of Adana under Mamluk suzerainty; their land is shown as Mamluk.
Marriage tie of 1367.
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

relations.explanation: Nominal Jalayirid suzerainty over Bayram Khwaja's Turkmen; often rebellious.
The Kayusid Shirvanshah Hushang is a Jalayirid dependent.
Pasture rivalry between the Turkmen confederations; open war later.
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

relations.explanation: Turkmen raids on south-eastern Georgia.
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

relations.explanation: Atabeg Qvarqvare I Jaqeli, a loyal great vassal of Bagrat V.
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

relations.explanation: Western Georgian lords (Dadiani, Gurieli, Shervashidze) under the crown; Imereti a royal province.
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

historical_end.how: Siemowit III dies; Mazovia splits into Płock-Rawa and Warsaw-Czersk.

relations.explanation: Siemowit III did homage for Mazovia in 1351; a Polish fief until it is partitioned on his death (1381).
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy

historical_end.how: Vytautas seizes Smolensk (finally annexed 1404).

relations.explanation: Smolensk has leant on Lithuania since Algirdas, but joined Moscow's 1375 campaign against Tver and was punished for it; a contested dependency.
Lubart, son of Gediminas and heir of the Galician-Volhynian princes, holds Volhynia from Lutsk; he made peace with Louis after the 1377 campaign.
sources: Frost, Oxford History of Poland-Lithuania I

historical_end.how: Vladimir is replaced by Skirgaila.

relations.explanation: Vladimir Olgerdovich holds Kyiv as an appanage of the grand duke.

historical_end.how: Vytautas expels Fyodor Koriatovich.

relations.explanation: The Koriatovich brothers hold Podolia from Kamianets under Lithuania, with ties to Hungary and Poland.
sources: Frost, Oxford History of Poland-Lithuania I

historical_end.how: Dmitry Olgerdovich defects to Moscow and fights at Kulikovo.

relations.explanation: Dmitry Olgerdovich holds Bryansk and Trubchevsk.
Tvrtko, crowned king in 1377, still recognises Louis as overlord.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

relations.explanation: Croatia, Slavonia and all Dalmatia (since Zadar, 1358) are governed by royal bans.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

relations.explanation: Royal voivodeship, probably under Ladislaus Losonci (from 1376).
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

relations.explanation: Jan III of Oświęcim holds his duchy as a fief of the Bohemian crown, like the Silesian dukes.
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy

relations.explanation: The Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order, with its own master; a military-order affiliation rather than vassalage.
Bishop Heinrich III Sorbom rules Ermland under the Order's protection; its chapter is not incorporated into the Order.
Prince-bishopric under the Livonian Order's protection; its chapter is incorporated into the Order.

Self-governing Hanse town. The Order forced it to submit in 1330; the papal settlement of 1366 is read by some as restoring the archbishop's lordship (taken here), by others as leaving the Order dominant.
Mikhail II holds Tver by the khan's patent and pays tribute; he sought Mamai's yarlyk for Vladimir in 1371 and 1375.
Ryazan pays the Horde and is the first land the steppe strikes; Mamai ravages it in the autumn of 1378.
Nizhny killed Mamai's envoys in 1374 and was punished by Tatar raids (Pyana 1377, a second sack in 1378); tribute contested.
The Orthodox principality of Gothia round Mangup is tributary to the Horde; its prince in 1378 is not known.
Caffa, Soldaia (1365) and Cembalo (1357) under the consul of Caffa; held by grant of the khans, who still claim dues.
Bobrok's campaign of 1376 forced the Bulgar emirs Hasan and Muhammad Sultan to pay Moscow and Nizhny and accept Russian customs men.
The Pronsk branch holds under Ryazan but leans to Moscow; Daniil of Pronsk led a regiment for Dmitry at the Vozha.
Rostov's princes (two branches) are Muscovite satellites.
Yaroslavl's princes are Muscovite satellites; they fought for Moscow in 1375 and 1380.
Vladimir Andreyevich the Bold, Dmitry's cousin and by treaty his 'younger brother', holds Serpukhov and Borovsk.

historical_end.how: Mamai is beaten at Kulikovo and soon falls to Tokhtamysh, who sacks Moscow in 1382 and restores the tribute.

relations.explanation: Dmitry stopped paying Mamai c.1374 and beat his general Begich on the Vozha on 11 Aug 1378; Mamai prepares revenge. Moscow is the Horde's tributary in law but withholds tribute, so it starts as a war, not a subject.

historical_end.how: Truce of Trakai covers some lands; the war resumes and ends only with Lithuania's baptism and Samogitia's fate (1411/1422).

relations.explanation: The crusade: yearly Reisen into Lithuania and Samogitia, Lithuanian raids into Prussia.
The Livonian branch raids Lithuania jointly with Prussia.
Truce after the Polish-Hungarian campaign of 1377 that took Chełm and Belz; terms and dates poorly known.
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy

relations.explanation: Both claim Volhynia, Chełm, Belz and Podolia.
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy
Frost, Oxford History of Poland-Lithuania I

relations.explanation: The Order holds Pomerelia and Chełmno land; the Peace of Kalisz holds and the rivalry is quiet in 1378.
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy

relations.explanation: The Order and the archbishop contend for the city of Riga and the archbishopric's chapter (won by the Order in 1394).
Border raids; war in 1367-71.
Algirdas's wars on Moscow (1368-72); Lithuania gathers Rus lands Moscow wants.

historical_end.how: Moscow attacks Trubchevsk and Starodub; Dmitry Olgerdovich goes over to Moscow.

relations.explanation: Truce of Lyubutsk after Algirdas's last campaign.
The old struggle for the Vladimir title. By the 1375 treaty Mikhail calls Dmitry 'elder brother' and gave up Vladimir, but tries again with Tokhtamysh in 1382.
Kolomna and Lopasnya; Moscow beat Ryazan at Skornishchevo (1371).
Karelia and the Neva; the peace of Orekhovo (1323) holds after Magnus's crusade of 1348-51.
Genoa and Gothia contend for the coastal villages, ceded to Genoa by the Tatars in 1380-81.
Louis fought Vladislav I in 1375-77 and holds Severin; Radu I does not obey his claim to overlordship.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

historical_end.how: Peace of Turin: Venice gives up Dalmatia and pays tribute.

relations.explanation: War of Chioggia: Louis backs Genoa, Padua and Aquileia against Venice and wants Dalmatia confirmed and a Venetian tribute; when he formally entered the war (1378 or 1379) is unsure, so it starts as hostility.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

relations.explanation: Allied against Venice in the War of Chioggia.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

historical_end.how: Louis dies and the two crowns part.

relations.explanation: One king, Louis; Polish and Hungarian troops campaigned together against Lithuania in 1377.
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy
Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

historical_end.how: Jadwiga marries Jogaila instead.

relations.explanation: Jadwiga betrothed to William of Habsburg at Hainburg.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

relations.explanation: Mary betrothed to Sigismund of Luxembourg, margrave of Brandenburg.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

relations.explanation: Algirdas fought for Tver in 1368-75; Jogaila is Mikhail II's nephew.
Dmitry Konstantinovich is Dmitry of Moscow's father-in-law and junior partner; joint Bulgar campaign 1376.
Moscow is Pskov's protector through its prince Andrei Olgerdovich.
Andrei Olgerdovich, passed over for Jogaila, serves Moscow and fights for it in 1379-80.
Timur shelters and arms Tokhtamysh, grants him Otrar, Sabran and Sighnaq, and campaigned against Urus Khan himself (1376-77). Patron and client.

historical_end.how: Tokhtamysh, now khan of the united Horde, sacks Tabriz and turns on Timur.

sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane

relations.explanation: Timur claims all Khwarazm as Chagatai land and has held Kath and Khiva since 1373; Yusuf Sufi raided Timur's lands in 1376-77. Open war (the siege of Urgench) follows in early 1379.

historical_end.how: Timur besieges Urgench; Yusuf Sufi dies during the siege and the city submits.

sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane

relations.explanation: Timur campaigned against Qamar ud-Din in 1371, 1375 and 1376-77 and claims to restore the whole Chagatai ulus; Moghul raids hit Ferghana. No campaign is under way in September 1378.
sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane

relations.explanation: Pir Ali's son Pir Muhammad married Timur's niece; good terms until Pir Ali refuses Timur's summons to a quriltai in 1380.

historical_end.how: Pir Ali refuses Timur's summons; Timur takes Herat in April 1381.

sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane

relations.explanation: The shahs of Badakhshan submitted after the campaigns of the 1360s; Timur's suzerainty is loose.
sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane

relations.explanation: Shah Shuja took Tabriz after Shaykh Uvais's death (1375) and had to withdraw; both claim the Ilkhanid inheritance.
Sunni Herat against Shi'i Sabzevar; Nishapur and the road west are contested.
The long feud between Amir Wali and the Sarbadars over western Khorasan.
Mir-i Buzurg helped Sayyid Ali Kiya take Lahijan; two sayyid regimes on the Caspian.
Recurrent wars between the Mar'ashi sayyids and the Paduspanids of Rustamdar.
Sayyid Ali Kiya presses the lords of western Gilan; it ends at the battle of Rasht (1389), where he is killed.
Arab Shah destroyed the Russian army at the Pyana (2 Aug 1377) and sacked Nizhny Novgorod.
The Genoese seized Soldaia and the coast villages in 1365 and Mamai contests them; Caffa still holds its land by Jochid grant.
The old Jochid-Mamluk alliance and the slave trade through the Straits.
Rivals for the whole Ulus of Jochi; it ends at the Kalka (1380/81), after which the White Horde takes the Jochid throne.

historical_end.how: Tokhtamysh beats Mamai and unites the Horde (white_horde merges into great_horde).

relations.explanation: Rival holders of the Volga and Sarai during the Great Troubles.
Novgorod collects Yugra tribute irregularly (an expedition reached the Ob in 1364).
Pechora tribute, nominal.

facts.explanation: Kera Tamara, sister of Ivan Shishman, in Murad I's harem (date disputed: c.1371, c.1376 or 1380s).
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium
Inalcik, The Ottoman Empire: The Classical Age

facts.explanation: Byzantine civil war: the deposed John V (with Manuel II), imprisoned since Andronikos IV seized Constantinople on 12 Aug 1376, claims the throne. Historically he escapes in June 1379 and retakes Constantinople on 1 Jul 1379 with Ottoman troops and Venetian ships. Modelled as a succession dispute inside byzantium, not as two realms.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

historical_end.how: John V restored; Andronikos IV flees to Genoese Pera, made heir again in 1381.

facts.explanation: Francesco I Gattilusio married Maria Palaiologina, sister of John V; he backs John V.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

facts.explanation: Tvrtko crowned 'King of the Serbs and Bosnia' (26 Oct 1377) by Nemanjić descent.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

facts.explanation: Vuk Branković married Mara, Lazar's daughter.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

facts.explanation: Ragusan merchants carry the silver of Novo Brdo and Rudnik.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

facts.explanation: Ragusan trade in Bosnian silver and lead.
sources: Nicol, The Last Centuries of Byzantium

facts.explanation: Peter IV of Aragon claims the duchies of Athens and Neopatras after Frederick III's death (1377).
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

facts.explanation: Peter II and Valentina Visconti.
sources: Setton, The Papacy and the Levant vol. 1

facts.explanation: Venetian trade treaties at Ayasoluk (Theologo).
Venetian trade treaties at Balat (Palatia).
Genoese trade at Sinop.
Anna Komnene, daughter of Alexios III, married Bagrat V (1367).
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

facts.explanation: Maria Komnene married Qutlugh Bey (1358).
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

facts.explanation: Tabriz route trade.
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

facts.explanation: Tabriz route trade.
sources: Suny, The Making of the Georgian Nation

historical_end.how: Louis dies; Mary takes Hungary and the Poles crown Jadwiga (1384).

facts.explanation: Louis I the Great is king of Hungary and of Poland; Poland is governed by his mother Elizabeth (Łokietek's daughter) or a governor.
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy
Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

facts.explanation: Angevin claim since the murder of Andrew, Louis's brother; it becomes Charles of Durazzo's invasion (1380-81).
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

facts.explanation: Jadwiga and William of Habsburg betrothed at Hainburg.
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

facts.explanation: Mary betrothed to Sigismund of Luxembourg (marriage 1385).
sources: Engel, The Realm of St Stephen

facts.explanation: Algirdas married Uliana, Mikhail II's sister; Jogaila is her son.
Dmitry of Moscow married Evdokia, daughter of Dmitry Konstantinovich.
Andrei Olgerdovich, eldest son of Algirdas, claims the grand ducal throne given to Jogaila.
The Polish crown claims the Rus land Casimir conquered; Louis put it under Hungarian starostas in 1378. Jadwiga retakes it in 1387.
sources: Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy
Frost, Oxford History of Poland-Lithuania I

facts.explanation: Russian trade through Reval and Dorpat to the Hanse's Peterhof in Novgorod.
The Hanse's Peterhof in Novgorod.
Khanzada (Sevin Beg) of the Sufid house married Timur's son Jahangir (d. 1376) and then Miran Shah.
sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane

facts.explanation: Pir Muhammad, son of Malik Pir Ali, married Timur's niece.
sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane

facts.explanation: Caffa and the Genoese ports trade under Jochid grants.
Venetian Tana on the Don trades by the khan's privilege; disturbed by the War of Chioggia.
Slaves from the Kipchak steppe shipped to Egypt.
Tokhtamysh, a Chinggisid of the Toqa-Temürid line, claims the Jochid throne that Mamai (no Chinggisid) holds through puppet khans.

entities.name: Galicia-Ruthenia (Rus land of the crown, under Hungarian starostas)
